identification: Two hand-forged shingle splitters (froes), bush-made, probably late 19th to mid 20th century Tasmanian/Australian: (1) short broad blade (about 25-28cm) with angled/rounded tip, wrapped eye, on a long straight pale timber handle (about 80-90cm, likely a replacement); (2) long narrow blade (about 30-35cm) with angled tip on a tapered dark turned handle (about 55-60cm, looks original). Light surface rust, blades intact.
